description: Delay that can be clocked, with a filter in the feedback path and a reverse that plays the buffer backwards

params.text: Sets the delay time, 1ms at one end and 10 seconds at the other, halving and doubling as it moves
Sets how much of the delayed signal is fed back in, none at one end and all of it at the other
Sets the corner of the lowpass filter in the feedback path, 39Hz at one end and 11000Hz at the other
Crossfades the output between the dry signal and the delayed one
Each press switches the delay between playing forwards and backwards, and a voltage above 1V at the reverse input flips whatever the button is set to

inputs.text: Shifts the delay time, 1V halving or doubling it
Raises the feedback, 10V covering the whole of the feedback knob's travel, with the total held inside it
Shifts the dry and delayed balance, 10V covering the whole of the mix knob's travel, with the total held inside it
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the filter corner comes from its knob alone
The signal fed into the delay
A rising edge past 2V sets the delay time from the gap between edges, and with nothing patched the delay runs at a fixed 2Hz base rate instead
A voltage above 1V flips the reverse the other way from the button, and lets it go when it falls back

outputs.text: The dry and delayed signals mixed according to the mix knob

notes: the delay time is the time knob divided by the clock: a clock at the clock input replaces the fixed 2Hz base rate, so the delay follows the tempo.
